thread:
maria-support: FYI — org 6789 reporting a burst of 502s + timeouts against hosted inference in eu-west-2 (AZ2) starting ~02:12 UTC. Customer sees request latency jump to ~8s and repeated 502 Gateway responses. They attached curl output and a short trace.
ben-cs: got the forwarded logs. Alerts fired in our error-rate monitors at 02:15 UTC for route rwd-infer-eu-west-2. Customers on multiple API keys.
incident-bot: Incident INC-202603-az2-interconnect created by maria-support.
kevin-oncall: I'm on it. Quick glance at the gateway dashboard — 502 spike from 02:11 → 02:25 UTC, 95th latency up from 120ms -> 1.2s. Linking: https://console.redwood.dev/dashboards/INC-202603 (internal).
julia-eng-sre: running network probes from AZ2 edge -> transit. mtr shows intermittent packet loss 1-3% + high jitter on hop 4. Observed TCP retransmits and some out-of-order packets. Sample tcpdump captured TLS retransmit/dup acks. Snippet: ```# tcpdump -n -c 100 -i eth0 'tcp port 443'
02:12:18.123456 IP 10.0.1.5.54321 > 198.51.100.20.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:501, ack 1, win 64240
02:12:18.223789 IP 198.51.100.20.443 > 10.0.1.5.54321: Flags [.], seq 1:501, ack 1, win 65535 (retransmission)
```
sam-neteng: Confirming — our border BGP peer (ASN 65023) reported adj-flap around 02:10 UTC. Provider NOC says they saw microbursts on the interconnect and a short fanout change across ECMP paths. This can cause reordering and loss for a subset of flows. I've opened upstream ticket TICKET-98765 and flagged it as high.
kevin-oncall: Mitigation plan: 1) enable region fallback for the affected customer routes to prefer AZ1 hosts; 2) temporarily widen our gateway connection health thresholds to avoid immediate drain on slight packet loss; 3) start a small canary shift now and monitor error-rate. Rolling canary at 02:34 UTC.
maria-support: I've informed the customer that we initiated a reroute to eu-west-2 AZ1 and we're investigating with the provider. Asked them to validate if errors persist.
ben-cs: customer reported reduced 502s after the reroute but still sees occasional timeouts at 02:39 UTC. They asked for ETA and whether this will impact billing/SLA.
julia-eng-sre: Root cause (preliminary): interconnect microbursts + ECMP path churn -> packet loss + reorder -> TCP/TLS session instability under our pooled connections -> gateway returns 502/504 under backpressure. Short-term tech mitigations: increase idle TCP retries on our proxy, bump connection keepalive, and extend health-check grace window to avoid premature failovers. Long-term: work with provider on jitter mitigation and consider adding explicit path-aware balancing for critical flows.
sam-neteng: Provider NOC says they see repeated microbursts on the physical link and are performing a link-level debug. They've scheduled a maintenance shunt at ~04:00 UTC to stabilize. We'll keep our reroute until they confirm. Ticket updated: https://provider.status/tickets/98765 (internal link).
kevin-oncall: Action items for now: 1) keep AZ1 preference active until provider confirms stable; 2) support to draft customer communication and proposed credits if SLA breached; 3) eng-sre to capture full packet captures and add detection rule for >0.5% packet loss over 5m to trigger automated region failover; 4) postmortem owner assigned. Next update in 30m. :eyes:
ben-cs: drafting customer message now, will propose a short-term credit offer and explain mitigation steps. I'll CC legal if they push for extended SLA impact.
incident-bot: INC-202603 status updated -> mitigated (partial) at 02:45 UTC.
maria-support: Thanks team — once provider confirms stability we'll run a controlled revert and monitor for 60m before closing. Postmortem notes: add runbook entry for ECMP-induced reordering and include exact tcpdump/mtr commands for on-call. :white_check_mark:
